sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house fast in Lawrenceville?
sections.html:
Lawrenceville homeowners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take an as-is offer, and the best route depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close. The city is the county seat of Gwinnett County, about 30 miles northeast of downtown Atlanta, and the Census Bureau puts the July 1, 2025 estimate at 32,822 residents.

Gwinnett is one of the busiest property markets in Georgia, so a well-kept house with updated systems can attract several showings. A house with deferred repairs or a title issue often moves faster to a buyer who does not need a mortgage.

sections.h2: What does Census data say about housing in Lawrenceville?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 Census figures show a city with a median owner-occupied home value of $350,600 and median gross rent of $1,613. Of the 10,719 households, 47.0 percent live in homes they own, and the average household has 2.82 people.

  • Median household income: $61,561 (in 2024 dollars)
  • Residents who speak a language other than English at home: 41.4 percent
  • Foreign-born residents: 29.5 percent
  • Mean commute to work: 32.1 minutes

A seller with a diverse buyer pool should consider marketing in more than one language, because the Census count of non-English speakers at home is unusually high for a city this size.

sections.h2: How old is Lawrenceville and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Lawrenceville was incorporated by the Georgia General Assembly on December 15, 1821, making it the second oldest city in the metro Atlanta area, and it is named for Commodore James Lawrence of War of 1812 fame. A permanent courthouse site on the square was selected that same year. The courthouse standing on the square today dates to 1885, and the Gwinnett Justice and Administration Center opened in 1988 and was expanded in 2020.

The city covers about 13.5 square miles in central Gwinnett and borders Dacula, Buford, Suwanee, Duluth, Norcross, Lilburn, Snellville and Grayson. Older streets near the square contrast with newer subdivisions, so buyers often ask which era a house comes from.

sections.h2: What jobs and roads drive demand for Lawrenceville homes?
sections.html:
Government, health care and education carry much of the local economy. The Census Bureau lists 2022 health care and social assistance receipts of about $2.2 billion and retail sales of about $1.68 billion for the city, a ratio that fits a county seat with a medical and court presence. Georgia Gwinnett College is inside the city limits, and the Presbyterian Church in America has had its headquarters in Lawrenceville since 1988.

For commuters, Georgia 316, U.S. 78 and U.S. 29 cross the area, and Ride Gwinnett and Xpress GA commuter buses serve the city. Gwinnett County Airport is partly inside Lawrenceville. The Census Bureau lists a mean travel time to work of 32.1 minutes, so buyers weigh road access carefully.

Gwinnett County Public Schools operates the public schools. Within the city limits are Benefield, Margaret Winn Holt, Jenkins and Lawrenceville Elementary, Jordan Middle, and Central Gwinnett and Discovery High Schools, plus the Phoenix alternative school. Jenkins feeds Jordan Middle and then Central Gwinnett, while Benefield feeds Richards Middle and then Discovery.

Some parts of the city are zoned to schools outside the limits, such as Simonton and Cedar Hill Elementary, and one northern subdivision is zoned to Collins Hill High. School zoning follows the address, so tell buyers to verify the zone with the district before relying on your listing.

sections.h2: How are Lawrenceville property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Lawrenceville has billed its own city property tax since tax year 2021, so a seller deals with two bills: one from Gwinnett County and one from the City Finance Department. The city's 2026 millage rate is 3.26 mills, and a mill is one dollar of tax on every thousand dollars of assessed value. Assessed value is 40 percent of the fair market value set by the Gwinnett Board of Assessors.

The city offers a basic homestead exemption of $20,000 off assessed value, which does not apply to debt service levies. Interest runs monthly at the prime rate plus 3 percent on late bills, with a 5 percent penalty every 120 days up to 20 percent. Ask the Finance Department at 678-407-6675 for the current due date, and make sure your closing attorney checks both bills.

sections.h2: How do I claim a Gwinnett homestead exemption?
sections.html:
You apply with the Gwinnett Tax Commissioner by April 1, and you must own and occupy the house as your primary residence on January 1 of that year. The county's release says no exemption is granted automatically, and once granted it does not need to be renewed each year. Applications can be made online at GwinnettTaxCommissioner.com/apply.

If you are selling, the exemption simply ends when you transfer title. Do not assume the buyer inherits it.

Permits are issued by the Planning and Development Department through the city's Licensing, Permits and Plans portal, where registration is free. A building permit is required for electrical, mechanical, plumbing, occupancy and structural work, and a Certificate of Occupancy must be obtained before a building is used or modified.

Permits can only be issued for land that is a buildable lot of record, meaning it was recorded with the Gwinnett Clerk of Superior Court before June 2, 1970 or appears on an approved and recorded plat. Sewer, water and septic permits come from Gwinnett County, not the city. Ask Planning and Development at 678-407-6583 about any open permit before you list.

sections.h2: What does Georgia charge to transfer a deed?
sections.html: Georgia sets its transfer tax at $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. The seller is legally liable, and the tax must be paid before the Clerk of Superior Court will record the deed.

faqs.q: Does Lawrenceville bill its own property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Beginning with tax year 2021, the City of Lawrenceville bills and collects its own property tax, separate from the Gwinnett County bill. The Finance Department's number is 678-407-6675.

faqs.q: What is the Lawrenceville millage rate?
faqs.a: The city's 2026 millage rate is 3.26 mills, which means $3.26 of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value. That covers the city levy only, not Gwinnett County or school taxes.

faqs.q: When is the Gwinnett homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. The Tax Commissioner says you must own and live in the home on January 1, and once an exemption is granted you do not need to reapply each year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Lawrenceville with an unpaid tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, but the balance will usually come out of your proceeds at closing. Unpaid city tax can become a FiFa lien under Georgia law, so pay or resolve it before accepting an offer.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell my Lawrenceville house?
faqs.a: The city's permit list covers construction, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and occupancy work, not the act of selling, but open permits can slow a buyer's loan and title work. Contact Planning and Development to confirm any permit on the property was closed out.
